sources.articleTitle: Centre extends ban on Zakir Naik's Islamic Research Foundation for 5 years
MHA declares Zakir Naik’s Islamic Research Foundation unlawful for another five years

headline: Indian Government Extends Ban On Islamic Research Foundation Again
seoTitle: India Extends Islamic Research Foundation Ban
metaDescription: The Indian Ministry of Home Affairs has extended the ban on the Islamic Research Foundation for five more years, marking the third such extension.
aiSummaryBullets: The Indian Ministry of Home Affairs has formally extended the prohibition of the Islamic Research Foundation.
This latest directive marks the third time authorities have prolonged the ban against the organization.
The entity, associated with Zakir Naik, has been subject to government restrictions since it was first designated unlawful in 2016.
aiContextParagraph: The Islamic Research Foundation, founded by Zakir Naik, was originally declared an unlawful association by the Indian government in 2016 under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act. Since that initial designation, federal authorities have consistently renewed the restrictive measures against the organization. The most recent decision by the Ministry of Home Affairs marks the third five-year extension, ensuring that the group remains prohibited under domestic law. This series of renewals follows initial investigations and regulatory actions taken by government agencies nearly a decade ago. The organization continues to operate under this legal status, which prevents it from conducting formal activities or maintaining sanctioned operations within the country. The government's decision to maintain this stance reflects its ongoing regulatory approach toward the foundation, which has remained a subject of federal oversight since the mid-2010s.
whyItIsViral: The story is trending due to coordinated reports from major national news outlets following the official government notification of the extension.
